code: PROMIS Satisfaction with Social Roles v2.0 8a
name: PROMIS Satisfaction with Social Roles and Activities Short Form 8a
developer: PROMIS Health Organization and PROMIS Cooperative Group; social health item banks by Hahn, DeWalt, Bode and colleagues (2014); distributed by HealthMeasures (Northwestern University)
construct: Satisfaction with performance of usual social roles and activities, including work, family and leisure responsibilities.

items.text: I am satisfied with my ability to do things for my family
I am satisfied with my ability to do things for fun with others
I feel good about my ability to do things for my friends
I am satisfied with my ability to perform my daily routines
I am satisfied with my ability to do things for fun outside my home
I am satisfied with my ability to meet the needs of my friends
I am satisfied with my ability to do the work that is really important to me (include work at home)
I am satisfied with my ability to meet the needs of my family

subscales.name: Total
subscales.description: Satisfaction with social roles and activities; unidimensional item bank short form.

scoring: Score each item 1 (Not at all) to 5 (Very much), no reverse keying, sum to a raw score of 8 to 40 (all items answered), then convert to a T score (mean 50, SD 10 in the US general population) with the HealthMeasures conversion table for Satisfaction with Social Roles and Activities 8a v2.0; higher T scores indicate greater satisfaction. HealthMeasures bands for positively keyed measures: 40 to 45 mild impairment, 30 to 40 moderate, below 30 severe (approximate; confirm in the current scoring manual). The raw to T conversion table could not be retrieved and is not reproduced here.
citation: Hahn, E. A., DeWalt, D. A., Bode, R. K., Garcia, S. F., DeVellis, R. F., Correia, H., & Cella, D. (2014). New English and Spanish social health measures will facilitate evaluating health determinants. Health Psychology, 33(5), 490–499. https://doi.org/10.1037/hea0000055
transcriptionNote: healthmeasures.net search pages are behind a form, the NIH HEAL CRF PDF redirected to a landing page and the HealthMeasures scoring manual URL failed, so no official PDF could be read. Items (text and order) and the normative answer list LL1017-4 (Not at all 1 to Very much 5) were transcribed from the LOINC panel 76800-2 (PROMIS short form - satisfaction with social roles and activities 8a - version 2.0). LOINC does not show PROMIS item IDs (SRPSAT codes) or respondent instructions for this panel, so instructions is left empty; the standard PROMIS instruction for this bank is a single line asking the respondent to mark one box per row with no recall period, but it was not seen in a fetched source. The T score conversion table was not retrievable from an open source and the interpretive bands in scoring are HealthMeasures' general guidance rather than text from a fetched document.
